security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences or safe argument-list command execution. Two documented shell command-substitution examples remain a real copy-paste risk, and the helper script can mutate GitHub state without a dry-run or explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: PR manager performs authenticated GitHub mutations without a dry-run mode.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run output and require explicit confirmation before creating PRs, editing reviewers, or adding project items.

remediation.issue: Documentation uses command substitution and an unquoted heredoc for generated PR body text.
remediation.suggestion: Use a temporary body file with gh pr create --body-file, or use a quoted heredoc and avoid shell evaluation of generated text.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts accept PR and branch inputs with limited validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate PR numbers and branch names, and use option separators where supported before passing user input to CLI tools.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated GitHub Mutations Lack Dry Run
semantic_findings.description: The PR manager can create pull requests, edit reviewers, and add project items through authenticated GitHub CLI calls without a dry-run mode or per-action confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited calls invoke gh pr create, gh pr edit, and gh project item-add using the user authenticated GitHub context. This is intended automation, but the lack of dry-run or confirmation creates a concrete workflow safety risk.

content.user_title: Review Pull Requests with Quality Gates
content.value_statement: Pull requests often miss clear review steps, test checks, and merge guidance. This skill provides structured PR creation, review, quality gates, and GitHub workflow automation.
actual_capabilities: Drafts pull request titles and descriptions from branch changes and commits.
Reviews pull requests with checklists for correctness, security, testing, performance, and maintainability.
Runs quality gate checks through included GitHub CLI and shell helper scripts.
Suggests merge strategies based on commit structure and review readiness.
Can auto-label, assign reviewers, and sync project boards when the helper script is run.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication for helper scripts that read or change pull requests.
Quality gate results depend on repository checks, test data, and available CI status.
The self-improvement quality check is optional and only works when that plugin exists.
Automation may change GitHub metadata, so users should review actions before running scripts.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Generate a clear title, description, testing checklist, and issue links before opening a PR.

use_cases.title: Review Code Changes
use_cases.description: Apply a structured review process across security, tests, performance, maintainability, and documentation.

use_cases.title: Manage PR Readiness
use_cases.description: Check CI status, test presence, PR size, and merge options before approving or merging.

prompt_templates.title: Review a PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a structured review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request 123. Check correctness, tests, security, documentation, and merge readiness. Give a clear approval recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a PR Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a new pull request from local changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request description for my current branch. Include summary, key changes, testing, risks, and related issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run Quality Gates
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate a PR before review or merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the pull request quality gate process for PR 123. Report CI, tests, security checks, size, and required follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Plan PR Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow automation with controlled actions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze PR 123 and propose labels, reviewers, project board updates, and merge strategy. Ask before making any GitHub changes.

output: CI passed and the PR size is within the preferred range.
Tests cover the main path, but edge case coverage should be added.
Recommendation: request changes until the missing tests are added.

output_examples.input: Create a PR summary for an authentication update.
output_examples.output: Summary: Adds token validation, refresh handling, and authentication middleware. Testing should include unit checks, endpoint coverage, and manual login validation.

output_examples.input: Should I squash or merge this PR?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: squash and merge. The commits include several fixup changes, and one clean final commit will be easier to audit.

best_practices: Keep pull requests small, focused, tested, and linked to related issues.
Run quality gates before requesting review and again before merging.
Ask for confirmation before running scripts that change GitHub labels, reviewers, or project boards.
anti_patterns: Do not approve a pull request when tests, security checks, or unresolved comments are still failing.
Do not use automation to hide unclear ownership, missing context, or large unrelated changes.
Do not run GitHub mutation scripts without checking the target repository and PR number.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide PR creation and includes a helper script. GitHub changes require the user to run authenticated commands.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.

faq.question: Can it post code reviews to GitHub?
faq.answer: It provides review guidance and examples. Posting requires GitHub CLI access and user-approved commands.

faq.question: Does it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It structures review work, but maintainers still need to judge design, risk, and product impact.

faq.question: What does the quality gate script check?
faq.answer: It checks CI status, test file presence, simple security patterns, and pull request size.

faq.question: What should users verify before running helper scripts?
faq.answer: Users should verify the repository, PR number, GitHub account, and every state-changing action.
